source.title: Direct Feedback Alignment Provides Learning in Deep Neural Networks

record.tranche_reason: Reports training error for back-propagation networks on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, bearing on whether networks fit the training data. Its optimizer and training method differ from V1's stated recipe.
record.gate_note: Training-error values are reported in parentheses only when higher than 0.1%; table cells without parentheses therefore indicate training error at or below that threshold, as stated in the captions. Rows cover the BP results relevant to V1. FA and DFA are different training methods and do not test V1's gradient-training claim; test-error results do not measure the claimed behavior.
record.test_reason: The study reports near-zero training classification error for randomly initialized convolutional networks on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 using back-propagation with RMSprop. This bears on V1 through a different optimizer from its SGD/Adam recipes.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase accurately reports the authors' conclusion about DFA, rather than BP: they claim it fits the training sets across their experiments and generally trails BP on test performance. However, 'fit' should not imply uniformly near-zero error: DFA's CIFAR dropout training errors are 37.6% and 69.8%. Proper initialization enabling deep BP training is cited prior work; its explanation of BP failure here is conjectural.
record.recipe_differences: Uses back-propagation with RMSprop and binary cross-entropy; V1 specifies SGD or Adam. The reported experiments use the paper's stated initialization schemes.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and architecture affect reported training error; dropout models have substantially higher training error in the CIFAR tables than the corresponding non-dropout multilayer models.

fits_no_version.finding: Fully connected BP networks have training errors of 2.5% and 38.7% with one hidden layer, 0.2% on both datasets with three hidden layers, and 36.7% and 66.8% with dropout.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-set fitting in fully connected tanh networks depends on architecture, dataset, and regularization under the tested RMSprop recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: DFA trains a 100-hidden-layer tanh network on MNIST to 0.12% training error, while BP and FA do not converge with the tested initialization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Direct feedback alignment can train very deep fully connected tanh networks under a recipe where BP and FA fail; this does not isolate initialization effects or test convolutional residual shortcuts.

record.peer_reviewed: 30th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NIPS 2016)
record.problems: The CIFAR tables give training-error values only when they exceed 0.1%, so lower errors are bounded rather than reported exactly. The study does not test V1's SGD/Adam recipes or corrupted and random labels.
record.rows_left_out: FA and DFA training-error entries in Tables 2 and 3 are omitted because those methods are not the gradient-based BP training method named by V1. MNIST results do not bear on V1's CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 conditions. Test-error entries are not training-error results.

untested.parts: SGD or Adam; corrupted or random labels; convolutional model-size comparisons; convolutional regularization comparisons; and effects of early stopping. A stopping rule is reported, but its effect is not compared.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious local minima, and extra student neurons.
Depth degradation in plain batch-normalized convolutional networks, identity-shortcut comparisons, special initialization of deep plain tanh networks, and Fixup.

Controlled initialization comparisons, signal or gradient propagation, and resulting training speed or trainable depth. Improved BP initialization is discussed through citations and conjecture rather than tested.
Learning rates relative to a measured stability threshold, curvature changes, catapult recovery, and edge-of-stability dynamics.
Batch normalization comparisons, higher-learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these versions. Remove the record's fully connected limits_scope and challenges verdicts. FA/DFA results and MNIST results were explicitly declared omitted, so they do not require missing entries. Test-error uncertainty does not establish uncertainty for the parenthesized training errors.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test SGD or Adam, corrupted or random labels, early stopping, or the stated smaller-model and regularized-recipe comparisons. Uses RMSprop and binary cross-entropy.
